issues.reason: The clause is a verbal passive of catch_up, and "a passive carries exactly the roles its active would", so the surface subject takes the active object's role (Theme by the unchanged-object default); Experiencer is reserved for the subject of a stative psych or predicate-adjective predication.
The entity-attached argument oblique must use "the preposition actually used — never a synonym head for a near-fit reading", and the sentence's complementizer is "to" ("plans to expand"), not "for".

gaps_confirmed: noun + to-infinitive complement ("plans to expand Wagerup") — the argument-PP rule for nouns names only prepositional complements ("a vehicle for V-ing"), so nothing states the head for an infinitival one
episodic (non-generic) bare plural subject — the determiner rule makes a bare plural the generic, which cannot express a specific past episode about particular plans
sentence-initial discourse "But" whose other endpoint lies outside the sentence — the connective rule needs two reified clauses, so the contrast is dropped
new_gaps: a subjective 's-genitive on a nominalization ("the project's impact on ...") — the instruction set routes only the of-phrase counterpart to the argument oblique, so the same relation lands in Possession or Of depending purely on surface genitive form
repair_summary: Re-roled the passive subject of the catch_up event from Experiencer to Theme (proof name catchup_exp -> catchup_th). Replaced the coined head For on the plans' infinitival complement with the surface head To (proof name plan_for -> plan_to).
notes: Nothing else was touched: the phrasal catch_up kept whole with no genus, the About/On/Possession chain on the impact nominalization, the participial adjectives heated/existing, and the past perfect with no second asserted event to order against are all per the instruction set. The local_resident fusion (with both its genus atoms) is a borderline classifier-vs-descriptive call the reviewer did not file, and no atom in it is false.
